Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: actionableFeedbackPolicy
candidates.comment: An actionable feedback policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a creative work or URL detailing its public engagement and feedback mechanisms. Also called public engagement policy, feedback guidelines, reader interaction policy. Examples: "A news organization's actionable feedback policy is its 'Corrections and Feedback' page.", "The company's actionable feedback policy outlines how customers can submit suggestions."

candidates.label: noBylinesPolicy
candidates.comment: A policy statement from a news media organization explaining when authors are not credited in bylines. Also called anonymous author policy, byline exclusion policy, uncredited author policy. Examples: "News Org A noBylinesPolicy 'https://news.example.com/bylines'", "Journalism Company B noBylinesPolicy 'Our policy is to omit bylines for staff editorials.'", "Media Outlet C noBylinesPolicy 'https://media.example.org/editorial-standards#bylines'".

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: publicAccess
candidates.comment: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: ethicsPolicy
candidates.comment: An ethics policy relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and the creative work or URL describing its ethical standards and practices. Also called "code of ethics", "conduct policy", "ethical guidelines". Examples: "News media organization ethicsPolicy 'example.com/ethics'", "Restaurant ethicsPolicy 'Statement on sustainable sourcing'", "Company ethicsPolicy 'CreativeWork detailing corporate values'". Distinct from diversityPolicy, which specifically addresses diversity and inclusion.

candidates.label: smokingAllowed
candidates.comment: An indicator of whether smoking is permitted within a specific place. Also called smoking policy, smoke-free status, smoking permitted. Examples: `Restaurant` smokingAllowed `false`, `Hotel Room` smokingAllowed `true`, `Public Park` smokingAllowed `false`.

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.

candidates.label: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
candidates.comment: A mission coverage priorities policy relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL stating its coverage priorities or public agenda. Also called: editorial policy, coverage guidelines, journalistic priorities. Examples: "News Outlet missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Focus on local news and investigative journalism'", "Broadcaster missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Public Service Mandate'", "Digital Publisher missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Transparency and Accuracy Statement'".

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: target

Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: targetCollection

Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". candidates.label: permitAudience

Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: targetPlatform
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."

candidates.label: targetUrl
candidates.comment: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."

candidates.label: targetName
candidates.comment: A textual name of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node name", "educational standard name", "learning objective name". Examples: "The alignment object has targetName 'Algebra I'", "The educational framework node's targetName is 'Critical Thinking'", "This targetName identifies a specific skill."

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: targetDescription
candidates.comment: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."

candidates.label: tripOrigin

Examples: "Flight tripOrigin 'London Heathrow Airport'", "RoadTrip tripOrigin 'New York City'", "Trip tripOrigin 'Home Address'".

candidates.label: itinerary

Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: arrivalPlatform
candidates.comment: A platform identification for a train trip's arrival location. Also called: train arrival platform, destination platform. Examples: "TrainTrip 123 arrivalPlatform 'Platform 7'", "TrainTrip to London arrivalPlatform 'Track 1'", "TrainTrip from Paris arrivalPlatform 'Gate C'."

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: distance
candidates.comment: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". Examples: "Exercise action 'Running' distance '10 km'", "Travel action 'Road Trip' distance '500 miles'", "Cycling activity distance '25 mi'".

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: legalAddress
candidates.comment: An official location relation between an organization and its legally registered postal address for administrative and tax purposes. Also called registered address, official address, corporate address, statutory address. Examples: An organization has a legalAddress of '100 Main St, Anytown, USA'. A company's legalAddress is 'Suite 200, Business Park, City'. The corporation's legalAddress is its registered office. Distinct from address, which is a general contact address, and branchOf, which is about organizational hierarchy.

candidates.label: cause

candidates.label: source

candidates.label: result

candidates.label: possibleComplication

Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: event

candidates.label: about

Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: associatedDisease

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: dissolutionDate

candidates.label: reservationStatus

candidates.label: dateDeleted

candidates.label: successorOf

candidates.label: replacee

candidates.label: countriesNotSupported

candidates.label: ownedThrough

candidates.label: supersededBy

candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: restockingFee
candidates.comment: A charge applied for restocking returned products, specified as a monetary amount or a percentage. Also called return fee, re-shelving charge, return processing fee. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` restockingFee `"$5.00"`, `Seasonal Return Policy` restockingFee `"15% of item price"`, `Electronics Return Policy` restockingFee `"$25"`. Distinct from `returnFees`, which is an enumeration of the *type* of return fees, not the amount.

candidates.label: returnShippingFeesAmount
candidates.comment: The monetary cost associated with shipping products back for returns. Also called return shipping cost, return postage fee, shipping fee for returns. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$7.99"`, `Large Item Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$25.00"`, `Free Returns Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$0.00"`. Distinct from `returnFees`, which specifies the *type* of fee, not the amount.
